content.text: Kaziranga National Park is one of Assam’s oldest and largest parks. It is also India’s pride as it hosts two-thirds of the world’s one-horned rhinos. It also has the highest density of tigers in the world. In 2006 it was declared as a tiger reserve.

Your trip to Kaziranga is incomplete without visiting the National Orchid Park. This park showcases beautiful orchids, handcrafted works from Assam, cultural shows and historical works of Assam. Local Fish is a must try being a local delicacy and much more. The fragrances of the orchids are sure to sweep you off your fleet. An ideal place to catch a glimpse of the culture and traditional lifestyle of Assam.

This forest is known for the rare exotic birds that flock here, like the Crested Goshawk, the Great Indian Hornbill etc. The kind forest guides can help you explore the uncharted areas of this park. You can hire a guide from the base of Kohara. It will take approximately 2 hrs to explore and witness the beauty of Panbari Reserve Forest.

Deoparbat Ruins located in Numaligarh, is an archaeological site. This is a popular place to visit in Kaziranga. The archaeological remains dates back to the 8th -9th century. The ruins portray the cultures of Assamese ancestors and people belonging to Ahom. While walking up to the hilltop you will see statues of the temple scattered. From this hilltop you can also get a view of the Numaligarh Tea Estate and Karbi Anglong Hills.

A beautiful fall that is well- maintained and peaceful, you might not want to leave this place because of its beauty and calmness. Though reaching this beautiful falls is a little hectic, you will have to cross five streams to reach this waterfall but it is worth it. The lush greenery and waterfall falling over it from a height is a spectacular site.
The travel time from Shillong to Kaziranga is about 5 hr 21 min (253.1 km) via AH1/AH2 in a cab. You can stop anywhere you want, since this is a half-day journey from Shillong to Kaziranga
